question.text: Total Expense Ratio (TER) for an equity MF is capped by SEBI at approximately:

explanation.text: The Logic: SEBI caps the Total Expense Ratio (TER) of mutual funds through an AUM-based slab structure under MF Regulation 52, with limits that decline as scheme size rises. For equity-oriented schemes, the maximum TER for the smallest AUM slab is around 2.25% for direct plans and roughly 2.5% on the regular plan side (direct + distributor commission), tapering down at higher AUM slabs. The Trap: A flat 1–2% range understates the cap for smaller schemes; 5% is well above any regulatory limit; "no cap" contradicts the SEBI TER framework altogether. Note: The Portfolio Managers (NISM-Series-XXI-B) workbook notes that mutual fund expense types and limits are subject to SEBI regulation and defines TER generally, but does not state the specific ~2.25% direct / ~2.5% regular slab caps on the pages checked. Those values reflect general industry/regulatory MF TER practice and should be verified against the current SEBI MF Regulations.
